rules.summary: The standard was obsoleted, replaced or withdrawn
rules.explanation: The body that issues the standard replaced or withdrew it, so code that follows it implements what others no longer do. Read the replacement the finding names, decide what the code has to change, change it, and record the review with kreateStandardsReview. Until then the finding blocks the gate.

rules.summary: The issuing body does not know the standard
rules.explanation: The body answered that it has no standard of this name. The declaration is most likely misspelt, or the standard was renamed. Correct the declaration in assurance { standards { } }.

rules.summary: A vendored test suite does not match what it pins
rules.explanation: The archive of a suite() no longer has the sha256 it pins, the pinned commit does not hold the vendored files, or a vendored file differs from its original, for example because a checkout converted its line endings. Tests that run on such a copy do not test against the suite. Restore the vendored files from the pinned archive or commit, or pin the archive or commit they come from; the finding cannot be reviewed away.

rules.summary: The vendored copy of a test suite changed since its review
rules.explanation: The digest of the files under the vendored directory of a suite() differs from the one standards.lock records. Someone added, removed or edited a file of the suite, or a checkout converted its line endings. If the change is a deliberate update of the suite, review it and record it with kreateStandardsReview; otherwise restore the vendored files.

An RFC that updates it, or an amendment or corrigendum of an ISO standard, changes what conforming code has to do without replacing the standard. Read the update, adapt the code and record the review with kreateStandardsReview.

rules.summary: A new edition, version or revision of the standard exists
rules.explanation: The body published a new edition of an ISO standard, a new version of a W3C specification or of Unicode, a new revision of a draft or a Unicode report, a new review draft of a WHATWG standard a new release of a specification on GitHub or a new commit of a test suite on GitHub. Compare it with the reviewed one, adapt the code and record the review with kreateStandardsReview.

rules.summary: The status of the standard changed
rules.explanation: The maturity of the standard changed, such as a Proposed Standard that became an Internet Standard, a Candidate Recommendation that became a Recommendation or an ISO standard that is to be revised. A change of status often comes with changes of content. Review it and record the review with kreateStandardsReview.

rules.summary: The standard has new confirmed errata
rules.explanation: The body verified errata of the standard, or holds them for its next update, since it was reviewed: an RFC erratum, an entry of the errata page of a W3C specification or a closed issue of its errata on GitHub. An erratum corrects what the standard says, so code written to the uncorrected text may be wrong. Read the errata the finding names, adapt the code and record the review with kreateStandardsReview.

rules.summary: A watched page of the standard changed
rules.explanation: A page that Kreate watches no longer reads as it did at the review: the url of a din() or document() standard, the errata page of a W3C specification or the watch page of a test suite. No service reports these changes in detail, so a changed page is the only hint. Look at the page, adapt the code if the standard or the suite changed and record the review with kreateStandardsReview.

rules.summary: The standard has new reported errata
rules.explanation: Someone reported errata of the standard that the body has not decided on yet, such as an open issue of the errata of a W3C specification on GitHub. They may be wrong, but they point at text that readers find unclear. Read them and record the review with kreateStandardsReview once they no longer concern the code.
